sections.title: Before reading: study Chapter 5 in How to read. An unanswered gate and a dark road

segments.text: 安不入門，寧待安。夜暗，燈在門外。門閉。安視燈，呼人。人不應。門內無聲。客持大書，持帙。紙有姓，客持紙。寧視路，安待人。燈明，路暗。客視紙。

inference_aids.alt: The closed gate gives no reply.
inference_aids.art_brief: Night at the new closed gate. An calls outside, Ning nearby; messenger holds large book/wrapper/surname note. Lamp outside, keeper unseen. Do not show parents, teacher, original An sheet, old leaves or a gate opening.

segments.text: 寧久待人，安坐。安閉目，客視門。寧呼安。安聞聲，開目。安應，寧取燈。火明，燈在手。寧視火，安視門。客開帙，視紙。帙有字，紙有姓。客閉帙，不讀紙。
寧獨行，至路。山暗，家遠。
寧：「北橋在水中。南橋遠。夜暗。」
segments.speaker: char-ning

segments.text: 安至路，寧待安。安視山，視燈。客獨立，持紙。路近，家遠。安不去，寧還。安還，至門。客視安，安視客。寧持燈，客急。
寧不入門，安不開門。客至路，視山。路暗，客還。寧立，待客。安視書，客至門。夜靜，路靜。客久待人，持紙。寧持燈，安視字。客開大書，視破葉。

segments.text: 客持大書，安取書。安持一書，客持紙。書在手，安視破葉。紙有姓，破葉無姓。客視姓，安視字。寧持燈，火近。客持紙，視火。寧持燈去，火遠。

inference_aids.alt: Light is moved to inspect the damaged leaf.
inference_aids.art_brief: Outside near the gate, An takes the large book from messenger for inspection under Ning’s moved lamp. Messenger retains wrapper and surname sheet. Do not invent readable writing, permission or ownership.

segments.text: 安持書，至路。安獨坐。書有破葉，安不閉目。寧至門，客視紙。紙在手，客視帙。安視字，不讀書。安呼寧，寧聞聲。寧應。寧持燈還。安立，寧至路。燈明，安視書。
客至路，安還書。客取大書，閉書。寧持燈，安取燈。寧視燈，安視火。安持燈，客持書。客開帙，視紙。紙有少字，帙字少。安視姓，寧視字。客閉帙，持紙。
客持紙，安視紙。紙在手，不在東岸。客視姓，不讀紙。
安持燈至門。寧至門，客至門。客持大書。安還燈，寧取燈。夜暗，燈不明。寧視火，客視門。安久待人，寧待安。客視紙。
安不入門，客待人。

sections.title: Their own voices cease; an unidentified reader is heard

segments.text: 寧視安，安視門。門閉，火不明。安不呼，客不呼。夜靜。客持紙，不讀紙。寧持燈，安坐。客持書。書在手。安視書，寧視路。
門內無聲，安視門。
安聞聲，立。寧聞聲，視門。客視紙，止。門閉，夜不靜。安視寧，寧不呼。客急。客持大書，安視書。寧持燈立，火在門外。安不入門。
聲在門內。安呼人，聲止。人不應。寧呼客，客應。安視客，客持紙。安不呼，寧不呼。
客持紙，視門。安視客，客不讀書。寧視安，安不讀書。安不入門，寧待安。
門閉。門內有火。人在門內，讀書。安聞聲，寧聞聲。

grammar.title: 安不入門
grammar.rule: 安｜不｜入門。燈｜不｜明。門內｜無｜聲。
grammar.note_en:
Study the Chapter 5 preparation in How to read before the story. It supplies the new meanings, controlled contrasts and explicit body/duration/location patterns. The traditional forms are the required script; pinyin gives modern Mandarin citation readings, not ancient pronunciation.

不 bù denies a following predicate, the part of the sentence saying what its subject does or is like. 安不入門 means “An does not enter the gate”: 不 stands before 入門, without a new ending or a verb for “do.” Compare 寧獨行, “Ning walks alone,” with 安不去, “An does not go away.” Different subjects do not change the negative’s shape. Not doing something need not mean being unable to do it: these clauses report actions and choices. They do not introduce a new word for cannot.

A quality can also be denied. 燈明 means “the lamp is bright”; 燈不明 means “the lamp is not bright.” The later 火不明, “the flame is not bright,” does not say it is extinguished. 明 míng selects physical brightness, not understanding or clarity. 暗 àn selects darkness. Do not equate 不明 with 暗 as universal synonyms. 夜靜, “the night is quiet,” contrasts with 夜不靜, “the night is not quiet,” when another sound occurs. The description follows the actual current sound scene, not a permanent quality of every night.

Keep absence separate from predicate negation. 門內無聲 means “there is no sound inside the gate.” 無 comes before the absent noun 聲; 不 instead denies an action or quality. Compare 門內有火, “there is a flame inside,” with 人讀書, “a person reads a book.” Neither having a flame nor reading identifies who owns either object. No general noun negation with 不 is taught.

呼 hū is calling and 應 yìng responding: 寧呼安，安應, “Ning calls An; An answers.” The answerer becomes the explicit subject of the next clause. 應 here is not the different yīng meaning should. In 安呼人，人不應, An calls for an intended person and that addressee gives no answer. The narrator can describe the unidentified person; An is not thereby given their name or role. A caller’s own companions can respond while the intended addressee remains unresponsive.

久 jiǔ modifies the waiting action in 安久待人, “An waits a long time for someone.” It stands before 待 in this bounded duration pattern. 獨 dú similarly precedes the action in 寧獨行, “Ning walks alone,” 客獨立, “the guest stands alone,” and 安獨坐, “An sits alone.” Nearby actions establish who has left whom. These uses do not teach every duration or adverb pattern, or the different only sense of 獨.

手 shǒu names a hand and 目 mù an eye or eyes. 安持一書，書在手 means “An holds one book; the book is in his hand.” The stated holder supplies the body reference; this is not permission for arbitrary possessive noun combinations. 安閉目, “An closes his eyes,” and 安開目, “An opens his eyes,” are physical actions. They do not assert sleep or poor eyesight. Keeping his eyes open during the inspection connects the action with attention to the writing. Follow the lamp’s holder as well as the book’s: light moves away, An calls Ning, she answers and returns with it. The book explicitly returns to the messenger before the group regathers at the gate.

The messenger’s 急, jí, “Urgent,” is an attributed report. 客急 presents him as pressed for a prompt response, rather than declaring him angry or naming an unseen commission. The context is the wait with his recovered sheet. It is not a general licence for 急 as quickly. His report and possession do not identify the ultimate owner of the book, sheet or lamp.

門內 mén nèi, “inside the gate,” is the newly supported counterpart of 門外, “outside the gate.” Only this bounded interior expression is taught here. In 聲在門內, “the sound is inside the gate,” location is explicit. The narrator eventually says 人讀書, “a person reads a book,” while 安聞聲, “An hears the sound.” These are separate clauses, not a perception complement meaning hear somebody perform an action. The reader of the story receives the anonymous reading fact; An and Ning hear it without acquiring the person’s identity. The gate stays closed and nobody enters. The next scene must establish any opening or meeting on the page.

After 聲止, “the sound stops,” a later sentence states the inside reading and fresh hearing. Read that new event in narrative sequence: the sound has resumed after the outside calls. The text does not need a new Chinese temporal connector to state those successive events.

Numbered cues: 1: teacher does not call, bù; 2: mother does not open her eyes, bù; 3: the flame is not bright, bù; 4: the road is not dark, bù.

C.title: Pensa C — Follow the wait, the light and the unheard answer
C.instruction: Continue each scene cue with complete Chinese statements supported by the reading. Retrieve an event, decision or contrast beyond the cue. No bare name, yes/no, guessed owner, keeper or permission.

items.rubric: Recall the absence of a reply and/or An’s non-entry. A named person or a repeated call alone is insufficient. No keeper identity.

model_answers: 寧：「北橋在水中。南橋遠。夜暗。」安不去，寧還。
items.rubric: Recall the remembered route constraint or the decision to return/wait rather than continue. Do not claim a newly observed bridge or an unmentioned crossing.

model_answers: 書有破葉，紙有姓。書在手，客持紙。
items.rubric: Distinguish the book’s damaged leaf from the surname-bearing sheet, or retrieve the explicit custodian contrast. No owner or unknown surname reading.

model_answers: 安不讀書。安呼寧，寧應。寧持燈還。
items.rubric: Retrieve the call, reply and/or return of the lamp that reconnects the people and light. Do not invent inability or permission.

model_answers: 門閉，安不入門。安久待人。
items.rubric: Retrieve the continued waiting/non-entry at the closed gate in a complete sentence; merely naming the lamp is insufficient.

items.prompt: 客不讀書，安不讀書。聲、人：
model_answers: 聲在門內。人讀書，安聞聲。
items.rubric: Require the inside reading/sound beyond the cue’s outside non-reading. Narrator states an unidentified person reads inside; An hears, without identifying the person or book owner.
